translationRepairs: In Qianlong 36 (1771), the Gepusizhai headman Jielangkazi Suonuomu seized the chieftain's stockade at Gepusizhai and murdered Chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai once again sent Yuanjun to deliver an imperial proclamation.

In Qianlong 36 (1771), the Gepusizhai headman, allied with Langka's son Suonuomu, seized the chieftain's stockade at Gepusizhai and murdered Chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai once again sent Yuanjun to deliver an imperial proclamation.
革布什咱頭人結郎卡子索諾木 parses as the Gepusizhai headman allying with Langka's son Suonuomu; fusing 結 into the false name Jielangkazi is a real error, and the proposed English is accurate.

In the thirty-sixth year, the Gepusizhai headman Jielangkazi Suonuomu seized the official stockade of Gepusizhai and killed the chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai again ordered Yuanjun to go and proclaim instructions.

In the thirty-sixth year, the Gepusizhai headman allied with Langka's son Suonuomu, seized the official stockade of Gepusizhai and killed the chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai again ordered Yuanjun to go and proclaim instructions.
Literal likewise misreads 結郎卡子索諾木 as one name; 結 is the verb 'ally with' and 郎卡子索諾木 is Langka's son Suonuomu.
As a provincial official attached to the campaign, Chengpei should never have been involved.
As a Board secretary attached to the campaign, Chengpei should never have been involved.
承霈以曹司從軍 uses 曹司 for a Six Boards departmental post; 'provincial official' is wrong, and 'Board secretary' correctly names the office.
Chengpei, as a provincial official accompanying the army, should not have been involved in this affair.
Chengpei, as a Board secretary accompanying the army, should not have been involved in this affair.
Literal repeats the 曹司 error; Board secretary is the accurate rendering of that metropolitan departmental post.

The rebels resisted fiercely. Cong directed his troops in an uphill assault, was struck by a musket ball, and died in battle. The entire force was destroyed. Among those who died with him were Company Commanders Zhang Qingshi and Chen Dingguo and twenty-five others.

The rebels resisted fiercely. Cong directed his troops in an uphill assault, was struck by a musket ball, and died in battle. The entire force was destroyed. Among those who died with him were Company Commanders Zhang Qingshi and Chen Dingguo and others, twenty-five in all.
同死者…等二十五人 totals twenty-five dead including the named officers; 'and twenty-five others' inflates the count, and the proposed fix matches the Chinese.
Serving as a battalion commander under Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign, he distinguished himself and rose through successive promotions to regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.

Serving as a company commander (qianzong) under Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign, he distinguished himself and rose through successive promotions to regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
千總 is the Qing company-level rank qianzong, not a battalion commander; the proposed rank label is correct.
As a battalion commander he followed Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign with merit, and through accumulated promotions reached regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
As a company commander (qianzong) he followed Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign with merit, and through accumulated promotions reached regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
Literal likewise over-ranks 千總 as battalion commander; company commander (qianzong) is required.

He then served under Chengdu General Te Cheng'e at Jiangka, hunting bandits, besieging the rebel stockade at Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many enemies. He was promoted to deputy vice general for distinguished service.

He then served under Chengdu General Te Cheng'e at Jiangka, hunting bandits, besieging the rebel stockade at Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many enemies. He was promoted to deputy vice general of the Maogong Brigade.
擢懋功協副將 names the Maogong Brigade post; replacing that unit with 'for distinguished service' invents merit language and drops the office designation.

Soon afterward he followed Chengdu General Te Cheng'e in stationing troops at Jiangka, capturing bandits, besieging the rebel stockade of Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many rebels. He was promoted to deputy vice general with merit.

Soon afterward he followed Chengdu General Te Cheng'e in stationing troops at Jiangka, capturing bandits, besieging the rebel stockade of Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many rebels. He was promoted to deputy vice general of the Maogong Brigade.
Literal 'with merit' likewise invents wording absent from 擢懋功協副將 and omits the Maogong Brigade; the proposed office title is complete.
He took Kayai as well and opened the route to Jiamu.
He took Kayai as well and captured Tongjiamu.
又克卡丫，取通甲木 pairs two captures; 通甲木 is the place Tongjiamu, not 'opened the route to Jiamu', and the following sentence's 甲木 is a related but separate place name.
He again captured Kayai and opened the route to Jiamu.
He again captured Kayai and took Tongjiamu.
Literal likewise should take 通甲木 as the place Tongjiamu under 取, parallel to 克卡丫.
He was soon promoted to Regional Commander of Sichuan.
He was soon promoted to Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
After 遷松潘鎮總兵, 旋擢四川提督 is a promotion to tidu; Regional Commander conflates 提督 with 總兵, and Provincial Military Commander is correct.
He was soon promoted to Regional Commander of Sichuan.
He was soon promoted to Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
Literal likewise mislabels 四川提督 as Regional Commander; Provincial Military Commander is required.
In Qianlong 38 (1773), he was again appointed Regional Commander of Sichuan.
In Qianlong 38 (1773), he was again appointed Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
复為四川提督 restores the tidu post, not a regional commander (總兵) appointment.
In the thirty-eighth year, he was again appointed Regional Commander of Sichuan.
In the thirty-eighth year, he was again appointed Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan.
Literal repeats the same 提督/總兵 conflation; Provincial Military Commander is the correct office.
During a blizzard, Tianbi led his men in a stealthy crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and struck Senggesang and Sedakela;
During a blizzard, Tianbi led his men in a stealthy crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and struck Senggesang to relieve Sedakela;
色達克拉 is the Qing-protected Ekezhi chieftain under siege (s0120), not a co-target with rebel Senggesang; the proposal rightly rejects co-attack wording but wrongly turns Sedakela into a place.
A great wind and snowstorm came. Tianbi led troops in a secret crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and attacked Senggesang and Sedakela;
A great wind and snowstorm came. Tianbi led troops in a secret crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and attacked Senggesang to relieve Sedakela;
Literal likewise must not treat Sedakela as an attack co-object or as a place-name; the action is striking Senggesang to relieve the besieged chieftain.

After Jinchuan was pacified, Qitu Gela'ersijia was captured and brought to the emperor at Rehe. At court interrogation he testified fully to Tianbi's fierce fighting at the moment of death. Lian was pardoned and allowed to return, and was appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

After Jinchuan was pacified, Qitu Gela'ersijia was captured and sent to the emperor's traveling palace at Rehe. At court interrogation he testified fully to Tianbi's fierce fighting at the moment of death. Lian was pardoned and allowed to return, and was appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
傳送熱河行在 specifies the emperor's traveling palace at Rehe; idiomatic 'brought to the emperor at Rehe' drops 行在, and the proposed wording restores it.

In the twelfth month Fukang'an's army arrived and the siege of Jiayi was lifted. Daji went out to welcome him, but—thinking himself high in merit after receiving a peerage and still recovering from the siege—he was too harried to perform the full ceremony of presenting arms and armor. Fukang'an took offense and impeached Daji for deceit, deep Green Standard Army corruption, and unreliability.

In the twelfth month Fukang'an's army arrived and the siege of Jiayi was lifted. Daji went out to welcome him, but—thinking himself high in merit after receiving a peerage and reward, and still within the besieged city—he was too harried to perform the full ceremony of presenting arms and armor. Fukang'an took offense and impeached Daji for deceit, deep Green Standard Army corruption, and unreliability.
拜爵賞 is peerage and reward, and 又在圍城中 means still inside the besieged city; 'recovering from the siege' invents a recovery state and omits the reward.
